_doc: Adaptive firing-cadence policy for the autonomous judgment loop. The loop re-evaluates this each run from cost vs. benefit. Not a fixed rule.
rationale: Provisional optimum. Measured $3.30/run; 3x/day x 30d ~= $297 ~= entire ¥50k target -> not economically rational. Free Actions layer covers fast event detection + immediate reactions between daily runs.
off_cycle_run_gate: expected marginal benefit > marginal AI cost

recommended_change.reason: Official period baseline of 1x/day remains rational (per-run cost small relative to the ¥50k target; the free Actions layer covers routine polling). 2026-09-01: an off-cycle run WAS justified and taken when the Etsy shop capability was granted mid-day -- this is exactly the kind of event the off_cycle_trigger_events list anticipated (new_capability_granted), and same-day thinking materially changed the outcome (built the entire publish pipeline instead of waiting for the next scheduled fire). Once the Etsy OAuth grant lands, another off-cycle run to trigger the publish Action and verify the result is also likely justified for the same reason -- a real sale or a listing going live is worth reacting to same-day, not next-day.
recommended_change.reaffirmed: 2026-09-01T12:30Z: two off-cycle runs taken today (owner blocker-classification correction, then Etsy capability grant) -- both met the gate (expected benefit > marginal ~$0.50-1.50 cost). Standing 1x/day baseline is unchanged; this is normal event-triggered variance around it, not a frequency change.

history.reason: Etsy shop capability granted mid-day; re-diagnosed the bottleneck and built the publish pipeline same-day rather than waiting for the next scheduled 20:07 JST fire
